title: Weighted graph as a 2D adjacency matrix
summary: Build a square matrix of edge weights for vertices 0 through n−1. None marks a missing edge, and the last weight supplied for a pair wins.
code: for source, target, weight in edges:
triggers: dense graph with frequent edge lookups
look up the weight between two vertex indices
prompts: Build a direct-fare lookup for routes that may cost zero.
Store distances between pairs of terminals, mirroring entries when the connection is bidirectional.
invariant: Entry [u][v] stores the weight of the edge from u to v, or None when absent.
mantra: Allocate independent rows, then fill the directed cells.
pitfalls: Multiplying a list of rows repeats references to the same row.

anchors.name: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
anchors.trick: A distance table starts with the direct edge weights.

complexity.time: O(V² + E) to build, O(1) per lookup

mutations.explanation: Writing one cell changes that column in every row.
